info.name: Team 19 – Login, users and templates
info.description:
Hana Fady, issue #11. Tests the login, token, user-account and template API, including the security rules from docs/security/threat-model.md.

How to run (easiest): in backend/, start the API with npm run dev, then in a second terminal run npm run postman. It creates a temporary dev Admin with a random password, runs this collection with Newman and deactivates the Admin afterwards (backend/scripts/postman.js).

In the Postman app instead: start the API (npm run dev), create an environment with adminEmail and adminPassword for an Admin on DEV (mark the password as secret), import this file and run the whole collection with the Collection Runner, in order. Requests share values (tokens, ids) while the run lasts.

Result on local dev (23 Nov 2026): 54 requests, 103 assertions, 0 failed.

Safety: it refuses to run against the live API, never stores credentials or tokens in this file (they live in the environment and in run-only variables), and creates only @example.test users, which it deactivates at the end.

exec: // 1. Never run against the live site: this collection creates and changes data.
throw new Error('This collection changes data. Run it against your local API (dev database), not the live site.');
// 2. One id per run, used in test emails and titles so runs never clash.

item.name: "alg: none" token claiming to be the Admin -> 401

exec: // A token with no signature that says it is the Admin. The API only accepts HS256.
b64({ sub: String(pm.variables.get('adminId')), iss: 'onboarding-portal-api', aud: 'onboarding-portal', iat: now, exp: now + 600 }) + '.');
pm.test('message: Invalid or expired token', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().error).to.eql('Invalid or expired token'));
// Take the real Admin token and change the user id inside it; the signature no longer matches.
pm.test('message: Invalid or expired token', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().error).to.eql('Invalid or expired token'));

item.name: Token in the URL instead of the header -> 401

request.description: Tokens are only read from the Authorization header, never from the URL (URLs end up in logs and browser history).

request.description: The token is still within its 1 hour, but the API reads the active flag from the database on every request.
